transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-22
Start: 09:30 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Emily (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood CSM), Marta (Orion Head of Platform), Ethan (Orion ML), Priya (Orion SRE), Daniel (Orion CTO)

Auto-summary: Weekly POC check-in focusing on Dedicated sizing and burst planning. Reviewed recent 10k rps simulation, discussed 95p latency creep under tail loads, tuned cooldowns, set a conservative 20% burst margin and agreed on a fallback model sequence. Action items and next steps captured.

Topics: throughput results, autoscale policy parameters, burst rehearse, cache behavior, VPC routing, audit/log retention.

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Samir (Redwood): okay hi everyone thanks for joining, I think we have most folks on. Quick roll call?
[00:00:11] Marta (Orion): Marta here.
[00:00:12] Ethan (Orion): Ethan -- hey.
[00:00:13] Priya (Orion): Priya, yes.
[00:00:15] Daniel (Orion): Daniel here.
[00:00:17] Emily (Redwood): Emily on the SE side.
[00:00:18] Luis (Redwood): Luis, CSM.
[00:00:20] Samir (Redwood): cool, thanks. Agenda: quick readout from the last stress run, tuning suggestions for autoscale, burst policy and fallback ordering, any VPC routing or security notes, and then agreed next steps.

[00:01:02] Ethan (Orion): quick note on the run — we did a 10k virtual users sim, targeted checkout flows that hit the text generation endpoint for order summarization. Average throughput looked fine but we saw 95p latency spike to ~980ms during sustained 2-minute windows. 99p also bumped intermittently.
[00:01:28] Emily (Redwood): that aligns with what we saw on the server side — there's some landings when the model spins up new workers and the batch sizes drop; the KV cache warmup is also a factor. I think there's an interplay of min instances and cooldown.
[00:01:42] Marta (Orion): when you say KV cache warmup, is that the prefix cache? we call it the pre-cache in our infra, so just making sure we're talking same thing.
[00:01:47] Emily (Redwood): yes same, sometimes transcribed as K V cash in logs, apologies. The prefix caching isn't fully primed for those synthetic sessions, so early tokens take longer.
[00:02:03] Priya (Orion): hm, so if prefix cache is cold, are we seeing heavy token reruns that blow out tail latency?
[00:02:10] Emily (Redwood): sort of — two things: cold cache plus minimal serving instances leads to small batches which hurts GPU throughput. Our suggestion is to raise min_capacity by one tier during business hours and reduce cooldown seconds from 300 to 90 for this workload pattern.
[00:02:26] Samir (Redwood): and for burst handling we recommend an explicit burst margin of 20% on top of the target p95 throughput, and then a fast fallback policy that steps down to a lighter model variant if latency exceeds SLA for >30s.
[00:02:40] Daniel (Orion): lighter model variant meaning smaller quantized model you host at the same Dedicated pool? just want clarity on ops complexity.
[00:02:48] Emily (Redwood): yes, exactly. We can host a 4-bit quantized variant in the same pool or in a neighboring pool in the same region. Fallback sequence is: full model -> high-quantized variant -> older distilled model, with logs emitted and a GC metric that flags quality regressions.
[00:03:05] Ethan (Orion): question on quality: do we have any automated evals to catch meaningful drift if we fallback? we don't want checkout summarizations to lose critical fields.
[00:03:14] Emily (Redwood): good call — we recommend adding a lightweight eval that checks presence of required entities (items, totals, address) and a heuristics pass that flags substantial token difference. It runs on a sampled stream and triggers an alert when accuracy dips below threshold.
[00:03:29] Marta (Orion): that seems ok. Cost question: if we keep min_capacity one tier higher and bump burst margin 20% what's the expected cost delta?
[00:03:38] Samir (Redwood): rough ballpark from our model: increasing min_capacity by one GPU slot is roughly +8-12% per month for this workload shape; the burst margin only impacts ephemeral capacity during short windows — with our recommended cooldowns you shouldn't see sustained extra spend. We'll send a detailed cost delta matrix after the call.
[00:03:57] Daniel (Orion): Daniel: we also need to confirm audit logs retention and KMS key handling for fallback variants — fallback cannot hit an external managed bucket that violates our data residency policy.
[00:04:08] Emily (Redwood): agreed. For Dedicated we can tie to your KMS and keep logs in your VPC-managed bucket; fallback variants will respect the same KMS and retention policy. We'll document the exact flow.
[00:04:20] Priya (Orion): networking question: the dry-run for VPC peering — do you have a runbook? we need to map firewall ports and load balancer sticky sessions.
[00:04:29] Luis (Redwood): Luis here — yes we'll share the runbook. Emily, can you note the LB sticky session recommendations?
[00:04:35] Emily (Redwood): sure. For this workload we prefer session affinity based on the session cookie, TTL 2 minutes to keep KV cache hits consistent. Avoid source-IP affinity if your clients NAT through a gateway.
[00:04:49] Ethan (Orion): got it. Another oddity we saw: during surge the GPU utilization dropped briefly which correlated with the 95p spike. suspecting small batches due to request routing.
[00:04:58] Emily (Redwood): yes that's the small-batch problem — runtime inserts empty padding to fill tensors; when you have many short sequences it hurts throughput. Workarounds: increase batch window to 25ms or use prefix batching; also increase seq length cap if possible.
[00:05:15] Marta (Orion): how do we balance batch window increase with latency SLO? we don't want higher median latency.
[00:05:21] Emily (Redwood): it's a tradeoff — for checkout flows we tuned batch window to 20–25ms and saw median up by 10–15ms but 95p improved by several hundred ms. That's acceptable given your 95p SLA target.
[00:05:36] Samir (Redwood): propose we run two parallel experiments this week: A) increase min_capacity and shorten cooldowns as Emily suggested; B) keep min low but increase batch window and add prefix warmup. We'll compare cost vs 95p improvement.
[00:05:49] Daniel (Orion): I like the experiments. Which one should we prioritize?
[00:05:53] Priya (Orion): from SRE view, shorter cooldowns may be lower risk to implement quickly. B needs more change in model runtime tuning and instrumentation.
[00:06:01] Ethan (Orion): I'll run experiment B in our staging cluster; Priya will pull the traffic generator for the 15m burst test.
[00:06:07] Marta (Orion): timeline?
[00:06:09] Samir (Redwood): Emily and I will push policy A into the Dedicated test pool by tomorrow, capture metrics over two business days; Ethan to run B and share logs by next Tue. We'll reconvene next Wed unless earlier issues.
[00:06:23] Luis (Redwood): adding cost projection to Samir's note — I'll prepare a short matrix to show delta for min-up, cooldowns and batch window changes.
[00:06:31] Emily (Redwood): quick sec, question from the group: fallback model hosting — do we want a separate pool per fallback or a shared pool with label-based routing?
[00:06:39] Daniel (Orion): prefer shared pool to reduce idle capacity, but need strict RBAC so only fallbacks run there.
[00:06:45] Priya (Orion): can we restrict which tenants or projects can spin up in that pool?
[00:06:48] Emily (Redwood): yes, we can set pool-level policies and namespace isolation; we'll document exactly what labels and service accounts are required.
[00:06:58] Ethan (Orion): one more — logs: can you append request IDs to the generation spans so we can correlate with our frontend traces?
[00:07:03] Emily (Redwood): absolutely, request ID will be propagated and present in trace output.
[00:07:07] Samir (Redwood): ok I'm going to read back the key decisions so we're aligned. Decision 1: raise min_capacity by one tier for business hours and shorten cooldown from 300s to 90s. Decision 2: adopt 20% burst margin; fallback chain of full->quantized->distilled. Decision 3: run parallel experiments A and B. Decision 4: run 15m simulated burst and upload traces. Decision 5: Redwood to provide cost delta and policy configs.
[00:07:31] Marta (Orion): correct.
[00:07:32] Daniel (Orion): confirmed.
[00:07:34] Priya (Orion): also confirm VPC dry-run and firewall checklist.
[00:07:36] Luis (Redwood): Luis will send runbook and checklist.
[00:07:39] Ethan (Orion): small aside — any thoughts on using a serverless style fallback instead of Dedicated neighbor pool?
[00:07:45] Emily (Redwood): serverless fallback can be more cost effective for super rare spikes but adds cold-start risk and KMS integration overhead; given your SLA we prefer neighbor pool fallback.
[00:07:58] Samir (Redwood): ok let's park serverless as a long-term option.
[00:08:01] Marta (Orion): any blockers from Redwood side to implement policy A tomorrow?
[00:08:06] Emily (Redwood): no blockers; I just need the final traffic window definition which Ethan will provide.
[00:08:11] Ethan (Orion): I'll send the JSON spec for the simulated checkout traffic by EOD.
[00:08:16] Samir (Redwood): perfect. Anything else?
[00:08:19] Daniel (Orion): nothing more from me.
[00:08:21] Priya (Orion): no.
[00:08:23] Luis (Redwood): I'll follow up on runbook and cost matrix.
[00:08:27] Samir (Redwood): great, thanks everyone. We'll capture action items and follow up.
[00:08:32] -- End of recording --
